text:
Gavin McKenna's first NHL season has become an argument about how the Maple Leafs are raising him. The first overall pick scored the winner against the Islanders on Nov. 23, on a delayed penalty with 11:05 left, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner, and it ended a nine-game losing run. Around it: Bruce Boudreau publicly criticising Jim Hiller's handling of him, and Toronto deciding not to loan him to Canada for the World Juniors, as Sportsnet reported.

The numbers explain why people are arguing. He has 7 goals and 15 points in 26 games, 8 of them on the power play, on 13.98 minutes a night. At five on five, though, Toronto has only 43.1% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on. His skating is already elite, top speed in the 97th percentile, while his shot is not. Daily Faceoff Toronto asked why Hiller is so reluctant to play him alongside Auston Matthews, and it's the question we'd ask too. Our numbers project about 47 points. For context, Macklin Celebrini and Connor Bedard both scored 0.9 points a game in their first full seasons.
headline: Gavin McKenna ends the skid, the debate rolls on
